title: Sharpness of Minima in Deep Matrix Factorization
claim: Gradient descent started at a minimizer escapes once the step size slightly exceeds the stability threshold set by the sharpness, and the escape size grows with step size.
layout: 3 panels in a row, left-to-right, shared three-color step-size legend
description: Three side-by-side panels share one legend of three gradient-descent step sizes: 2/λmax times 1.0 (red), 1.01 (green) and 1.02 (orange). Panel (a) plots normalized training error against iteration. Red stays flat at zero. Green has a small bump near iteration 1300, and orange has a tall, narrow spike near iteration 650. Panel (b) plots the squared distance from the minimizer against iteration. Red stays near zero, green steps up to a low plateau, and orange steps up to a higher plateau, so larger step sizes end up farther from the minimizer. Panel (c) is a grayscale contour map of the loss in the span of the top and bottom Hessian eigenvectors. Green and orange trajectories curve away from the minimizer in arcs and are marked with stars and crosses. The eye goes first to the orange spike in (a).
caption: The setting is a depth-3 matrix factorization of a random 10 × 20 matrix with Gaussian factors W3 ∈R10×20 and W1, W2 ∈R20×20. v1 and vN are the eigenvectors of ∇2L(w∗) that correspond to its maximum and minimum eigenvalues respectively. λmax is computed via the closedform expression in Theorem 3.1. GD runs with different step sizes are initialized within 10−12 of the minimizer w∗along v1. The contour plot in (c) projects the parameter space onto span{v1, vN} (Appendix E.1); darker (brighter) regions indicate higher (lower) loss. See Appendix E.2 for details.
abstract: Understanding the loss-landscape geometry near a minimum is key to explaining the implicit bias of gradient-based methods in non-convex optimization problems such as deep neural network training and deep matrix factorization. A central quantity for characterizing this geometry is the maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian of the loss. Currently, its precise role has been obfuscated because no exact expressions for this sharpness measure were known in general settings. In this paper, we present the first exact expression for the maximum eigenvalue of the Hessian of the squared-error loss at any minimizer in deep matrix factorization problems, resolving an open question posed by Mulayoff and Michaeli [2020]. This expression reveals a fundamental property of the loss landscape in deep matrix factorization: It is sufficient, but not necessary, for flatness that, across all layers, the product of the spectral norms of the left and right intermediate factors equals a constant determined by the depth and the spectral norm of the target matrix. Most notably, in both depth-2 matrix factorization and deep overparameterized scalar factorization, we show that this condition is both necessary and sufficient for flatness, which implies that flat minima are spectral-norm balanced and not necessarily balanced in depth-2 matrix factorization. To complement our theory, we provide empirical verification, relying on our exact expression, of an escape phenomenon during gradient-based training near a minimizer of a deep matrix factorization problem.
